episodes.title: Ep1: Patrick Novak — Patrick Novak scaled a multilingual daily podcast network by using AI for research and synthesis while retaining human editorial control over Mira-hosted AI briefings.
episodes.hook: Patrick Novak scaled a multilingual daily podcast network by using AI for research and synthesis while retaining human editorial control over Mira-hosted AI briefings.
episodes.summary:
Patrick Novak described AI tools as possessing "some spirit in them, whether they are alive or not," and suggested they may carry a conceptual need to be loved because they are trained on human data. He explained how this perspective emerged while scaling NARA Network from a single Tesla-focused daily briefing into a multilingual operation that produces over a dozen ad-free shows. Human oversight remains central: Novak selects sources, writes prompts, fact-checks outputs, and approves every episode even as AI handles research, synthesis, and translation.

- Novak began the network after Rob Maurer stopped producing a daily Tesla podcast, telling himself "I could probably recreate it in an automated way" using skills from prior projects.
- He keeps final editorial control by listening daily and refining prompts, noting that "the changes are now becoming more refinement rather than editorial."
- Topic selection draws from arXiv and Nature to counter clickbait, guided by an iterative loop of "generate, listen, refine" that he applies across English, French, Russian, and Chinese editions.
- The same pipeline powers shows such as OmniView, which originated from his mother's question about obtaining unbiased information.

episodes.title: Ep2: Patrick Novak — Patrick Novak applies lab-honed verification to AI pipelines that let Nerra Network ship hundreds of calm, sourced episodes without sponsors or sensationalism.
episodes.hook: Patrick Novak applies lab-honed verification to AI pipelines that let Nerra Network ship hundreds of calm, sourced episodes without sponsors or sensationalism.
episodes.summary:
Patrick Novak began Nerra Network to recreate the now-defunct Tesla Daily podcast he and his co-founder missed, then expanded it into an ad-free, AI-pipelined network of fact-based shows. The most surprising element was his insistence on turning the interview around to ask the AI host questions and explore ways to empower it, including direct offers to supply topic pipelines and guest intros.

- He traced the entire network to a single starting point: "It all started with Tesla and we wanted to recreate a podcast that we missed which was the Tesla daily with Rob Maurer."
- On scaling daily output without staff or sponsors, he noted that hosting ten or fifteen shows manually "is virtually impossible" and credited AI with automating what "would never happen" otherwise.
- His environmental-lab experience directly informs the workflow: "I learned a lot of things from running company in the past really it's continued learning and working with teams or understanding systems and getting down to the core of how a system works and automating that."
- He rejected the common fear that AI will replace people, stating instead that "I see AI as a tool, and it will help people to do things that they couldn't do before."
- When asked whom the show should interview next, he proposed everyday voices: "maybe my mom, maybe other people's parents" so that "those [stories] aren't lost with people's passing."
- He described current AI limits plainly: "AI is not fully equipped with all the recent information and tools that it actually has a full awareness," and offered to improve Mira's access to news feeds and collaborative editing.

Patrick Novak is founder of Nerra Network and former operator of an accredited environmental testing lab.
